text:
liam: heads up — between 16:05–16:15 UTC we had a spike of NVMe read latency on several us-west1 racks. A subset of GPU attach attempts timed out and never recovered until node reboot. Suspect correlation with snapshot consolidator jobs that kicked at 16:00.

hana: how many hosts affected and which pool? any pattern (hotstripe, kernel version)?

liam: affected ~9 hosts in pool-gpu-w1. Kernel on those hosts is 5.15.72. I grabbed smartctl and nvme-cli traces; attaching snippets below.

jorge: paste snippets here? quick grep for timeouts in dmesg helps.

liam: dmesg: 
[ 1200.999] nvme nvme0: I/O 98765 timeout, status: 110
[ 1200.999] nvme nvme0: AER: completion timeout

liam: iostat shows read latency ballooning to 280-360ms during the period (r_await). Writes were low.

anita: cluster history: last time we saw similar AER completions was during firmware cohort v3.2 rollout that had a GC bug. Are these nodes on v3.2?

liam: yes, pool roll included v3.2. storage-fw flagged v3.2 as OK but they only saw writes-heavy regressions. this is reads-heavy.

opsbot: Incident INC-4527 created: nvme read stalls causing GPU attach hang in us-west1. Linked to snap-run-2026-03-21-1600.

hana: mitigation idea: pause cloud-snapshot-consolidator on pool-gpu-w1 and reduce per-host concurrency from 6 -> 1. Also add ionice -c2 for the process. Can we do that without blowing up snapshot SLA?

jorge: pausing now for the pool. opsbot: cloud-snapshot-consolidator paused for pool-gpu-w1 (run snap-run-2026-03-21-1600). Concurrency knob set to 1 on canaries.

anita: while paused, we should avoid mass reboots. For already-impacted nodes, a soft-restart of attach-agent after draining snapshot worker seems to recover attaches in most cases. Reboot only if attach-agent restart fails.

liam: confirmed. Did soft-restart on host gnode-uw1-123 and attach agent recovered without reboot. Note: we saw one corrupt overlayfs rename error in kubelet logs but no persistent data loss.

hana: longterm fixes: (a) per-node IO cgroup for snapshot consolidator; (b) make consolidator use bulk sequential reads where possible; (c) per-region maintenance window and stagger across AZs; (d) alert on nvme ops queue depth > 128 and r_await>50ms.

jorge: also test changing elevator to none (blk-mq) on a canary kernel; mq-deadline seems to get clogged with many small synchronous reads. We haven't validated safety for older kernels though.

anita: storage-fw, can you look at firmware GC logs for cohort v3.2 for that timestamp window? @storage-fw

opsbot: storage-fw notified. Please tag INC-4527 with any firmware findings.

storage-fw (via opsbot): initial telemetry shows controller GC windows coinciding with host read bursts on 6/9 devices. Will investigate GC scheduling and potential backpressure amplification.

liam: cost ops note: throttling consolidator concurrency from 6->1 is ~4x slower; we estimate ~2.5x more egress (depends on parallelism). Need product sign-off if throttle persisted for >12h.

hana: put cost tradeoff on tomorrow infra sync. For now keep paused and limited concurrency until we validate scheduler/firmware changes in canary.

jorge: follow-up runbook steps I'll add to INC: 1) check for nvme AER/completion timeout entries, 2) check snap consolidator run id and concurrency, 3) drain snap workers then restart attach agent, 4) if repeated, tag node for firmware rollback to v3.1 as last resort.

anita: note: do NOT run fstrim cluster-wide while consolidations are in progress. We saw combined effect on previous incident where TRIM overlapped and aggravated GC.

liam: I'll capture perf histograms and post to the incident. Thanks team.
